text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate from rcu-paging-service detected across canary-2 (region eu-west). 5xx spike started ~2899990000. Triggering incident channel.

maya: I'm on it. seeing a big spike in streaming client errors correlated with the v3.1 SDK rollout canary. Canary traffic pinned to canary-2. First glance: streaming sessions get a 'cursor_mismatch' on paged responses.

ben: TL;DR — paging tokens appear to be incompatible between server v2.x encoding and client v3.1 decoder. Most errors are 400/422-ish client parse failures surfaced as 5xx upstream.

priya: digging into runtime logs now. I can repro locally with the v3.1 client against latest prod-staging. Paging token base64 payload layout changed (we added a 1-byte version header) but server still emits old token format for some instances during the rollout.

alex: customer impact — several PLG customers reported failed document search and chat history loads. Jordan, do we have number of affected tenants?

jordan: Support tickets started coming in ~+3m. I pulled 6 escalations so far, two enterprise customers (acme-corp, nordbank). All report pagination failing mid-session causing app errors. I'll open a status page draft.

maya: ok mitigation plan — 1) pause canary routing, 2) enable SDK compatibility FF to serve legacy tokens, 3) rollback canary hosts that have new SDK libs if pause doesn't help. Who can flip the FF?

priya: I can enable the compatibility flag on control plane in ~2m. It maps token decoder to accept both encodings. Patching code is trivial, but we need to confirm it won't regress other invariants.

ben: I'm spinning up a quick health check to validate token decode success rate once the FF is on. Will push a synthetic that paginates 1000 sessions across canary and control pool.

incident-bot: NOTE: Canary routing for canary-2 auto-paused by orchestration at 2899990120 due to error rate > 3*sigma.

maya: good — routing paused automatically. Priya, proceed with FF. Ben, run your synthetic after FF is live. Jordan, patch status page with "partial degradation for paging in eu-west; mitigation in progress". Alex, loop in account managers for acme-corp / nordbank.

priya: FF toggled ON: 'sdk_paging_compat_v3_1' -> true. Applying across eu-west control plane now.

ben: running synthetic now. initial results: before FF decode success ~ 68%. after FF toggled -> decode success ~ 99%. Latency stable. Looks promising.

jordan: Support update posted. Customers acknowledged, want ETA for full fix/rollback. Two customers requested immediate escalation calls. Alex is triaging.

alex: I'll join calls. Also raising that some customers are on pinned dedicated stacks — we may need to coordinate private deployments separately.

maya: next step: do we rollback the canary hosts that pulled v3.1, or keep FF and gradually resume traffic? Pros/cons?

priya: If FF fixes decode, we can avoid a full rollback (less churn). But we need to ensure the server rollout completes to produce the new token format consistently, otherwise we risk bi-modal token formats. Ideally we incrementally finish server rollout to v3.1 token emitter, then flip FF off after a compatibility window.

ben: risk assessment: leaving FF on masks underlying rollout mismatch; if any other component assumes the new header byte, we might get silent logic errors later. I lean rollback-first for safety unless customers push otherwise.

maya: operational decision: initiate a targeted rollback of the canary hosts that reported mixed token formats, keep FF on globally until we validate. Ben, coordinate rollback. Priya, prepare a postmortem note on the token versioning mismatch. Jordan/Alex, keep customers updated.

priya: creating a short runbook entry now and a git commit with the encoder revert for server agent instances. I'll add the diff in channel: ```diff
- encode_token(payload) -> b'\x01' + b64(payload)
+ encode_token(payload) -> b64(payload)
```

ben: rollback started at 2899990345 for 6 canary hosts (canary-2 pool). Monitoring.

incident-bot: DEPLOYMENT: rollback job #deploy-3891 started by ben at 2899990345.

ben: rollback completed for 6 hosts at 2899990480. Health checks green, decode success holding ~99% with FF enabled. Routing remains paused until we do a controlled resume.

maya: good job. Now we need on-call handoff in ~30m — my shift ends. Ben, can you take the remainder of the incident and coordinate with SRE night team?

ben: I can take it. I'll draft a short incident summary and action items.

jordan: support update: acme-corp and nordbank calls done; both satisfied with rollback + FF plan, asked for a postmortem. I've logged two follow-up tickets for dedicated/private deployments that need manual syncing.

priya: I'll run a migration job to normalize token format across all servers in staging before we resume canary. Also adding stricter schema checks to ensure decoder rejects unknown versions with clear logs.

maya: action items (summary):
- FF enabled globally: 'sdk_paging_compat_v3_1' = true (priya)
- Targeted canary rollback completed (ben)
- Synthetic verification shows decode success ~99% (ben)
- Support/customer comms and calls (jordan, alex)
- Postmortem + runbook updates (priya -> postmortem draft, ben -> incident timeline)
- On-call handoff to ben at 2899990600 (maya)

ben: I'll take over at 2899990600. Planning: keep FF on for 48h, finish server rollout with consistent token emission in a separate controlled change, then flip FF to off following canary validation. Postmortem will include a proposed compatibility policy: new token versions require dual-emission + 72h compatibility window.

maya: leaving notes in the incident tracker. Thanks everyone. Going to hand off to ben now.

ben: I'm on-call for this incident. Re-iterating timeline: root cause was a versioned token header introduced in SDK/server mismatch during parallel rollouts. Mitigation: compatibility feature flag + targeted rollback. Next steps: tighten release gating for token format changes and add automated preflight decoder tests.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error rate returned to baseline and customer errors reduced to normal after rollback and FF at 2899990775. Incident channel will remain for postmortem notes.

jordan: I'll collect customer impact metrics (number of sessions failed, affected tenants) and add to postmortem.

priya: posting a quick diff and link to the code revert PR: https://git.redwood/repo/paging/PR-4234

ben: thanks all. I'll open the postmortem doc and assign reviewers. Everyone, please paste any logs or notes into that doc.

alex: filed follow-ups with account teams. Notifying sales about potential churn risk for affected customers.

maya: thanks team. handing off. :heart:
